EMPLOYEES OLD-AGE BENEFITS (DETERMINATION OF COMPLAINTS, QUESTIONS, AND
DISPUTES) REGULATIONS, 1986 [Gaz
EMPLOYEES OLD-AGE BENEFITS (DETERMINATION OF COMPLAINTS, QUESTIONS, AND
DISPUTES) REGULATIONS, 1980
[Gaz. of Pak, Extr. Pt. II, 21 July 1980, p.
1398 [S. R. O. 760 (I) 80 dt. 19 July 1980.]
[Rules made by Board of Trustees in exercise
of the powers conferred by section 45 of the Employees Old‑Age Benefits
Act, 1976 (XIV of 1976.]
1. Short title and commencement.‑-- (1) These regulations may
be called the Employees' Old‑Age Benefits (Determination of Complaints,
Questions and Disputes) Regulations, 1980.
(2) They shall come into force at
once.
2. Definitions.‑-- (1) In these regulations unless there is
anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(a) "Act" means the Employees' Old‑Age
Benefits Act, 1976 (XIV of 1976);
(b) "form" means form annexed to these
regulations;
(c) "Institution"
means the State Life Insurance Corporation of Pak istan exercising and
performing the powers and functions of the Institution under the Act;
(d) "section" means section of the
Act.
(2) Words and expressions used but
not defined in these regulations shall have the same meanings as in the Act.
3. Nomination of Officers to hear and decide petitions.‑‑-
(1) The Head of the Institution may by Administrative Order nominate an Officer
or Officers of the Institution as he may think fit from time to time for
disposal of the petitions under section 33 of the Act.
(2) An Officer
nominated under sub‑regulation (1) of this regulation shall hear and
decide the petitions in accordance with the procedure laid down by these
regulations and the decision given by such officer shall be deemed to be the
decision of the Institution.
4. Complaints, questions and disputes.‑‑-- (1) Every
petition requesting decision on a complaint, question or dispute in respect of
any matter referred to in section 33 shall be made to the Institution for
decision, at one of its offices in form PI‑07, within six months of the
occurrence of the event to which such complaint or question or a dispute
relates
Provided that
the Institution may, in its discretion, entertain a petition after the period
of six months if it is satisfied by the nature and circumst ances of the case.
5. Procedure for hearing and deciding petitions.‑‑--
(1) On receipt of a petition filed under section 33, the Institution shall,
within three weeks of the presentation of the petition, fix a date, place and
time for its hearing under notice to the parties.
(2) Where on the
day fixed, or on any other day to which the hearing may be adjourned,‑
(i) the petitioner does not appear, the petition
may be rejected ;
(ii) the petitioner appears
but the respondent does not appear, the petition shall be hear ex‑parse ;
and
(iii) neither party appears,
the petition may be considered, and decided on the basis of the material
available on the record.
(3) The
Institution may, if sufficient cause is shown, at any stage, of the hearing of
the petition grant time to the parties or to any one of them, and from time to
time adjourn the bearing.
(4) The
Institution may, in its discretion, call for further information or examine any
person or persons or direct the parties to lead evidence for the purpose of
elucidating any matter in issue.
(5) The
Institution shall, within three weeks of the conclusion of the hearing notify
its decision by registered post to the persons concerned at the address shown
on the record of the case.
6. Review.‑--- (1) Any person aggrieved by a decision of the
Institution .may, within thirty days of the notification of the decision under
sub -Regulation (5) of regulation 5 make an application to the Institution in
form PI‑08 for review of its decision.
(2) The
Institution may, at any time, either of its own notice or on an application
made to it in this behalf within 30 days of the notification of decision under
sub‑regulation (5) of regulation 5 review, modify, reverse or confirm
decisions made by it.
